precepts.text: Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to thy neighbour; remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance. Sometimes brothers and sisters do something simple; wink at it. It does not always have to be a counsel for small matters. Abstain from strife, and thou shalt diminish thy sins. If thou blow the spark, it shall burn: if thou spit upon it, it shall be quenched: and both these come out of thy mouth. A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: we just read that Onias had to flee from Jerusalem to Syria. It hath pulled down strong cities, and overthrown the houses of great men.
precepts.point: Not only the Jews, but many also of other nations, took great indignation, and were much grieved for the unjust murder of the man, because Onias had a good report even among the other nations. The king was heartily sorry, and moved to pity, and wept, because of the sober and modest behaviour of him that was dead; and being kindled with anger, he took away Andronicus his purple, rent off his clothes, led him through the whole city unto that very place where he had committed impiety against Onias, and there slew he the cursed murderer. Thus the Lord rewarded him his punishment, as he had deserved.
precepts.why:
When Onias found out Menelaus was stealing vessels of gold out of the temple, he reproved him and had to run for his life, fleeing from Jerusalem up to the sanctuary at Daphne by Antiochia in Syria. Sirach shows what drives a man like that from his place.

“Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to thy neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.” Sometimes brothers and sisters may do something simple. Wink at it. It doesn't always have to be a counsel for small matters. “Abstain from strife, and thou shalt diminish thy sins: for a furious man will kindle strife”, and “A sinful man disquieteth friends, and maketh debate among them that be at peace.”

“An hasty contention kindleth a fire: and an hasty fighting sheddeth blood. If thou blow the spark, it shall burn: if thou spit upon it, it shall be quenched: and both these come out of thy mouth.” Your mouth has the power: you can blow on that spark and it will burn, or you can spit on it, let it go, and quench it.

“Curse the whisperer and doubletongued: for such have destroyed many that were at peace. A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation”. We just read that Onias had to flee from Jerusalem up to Syria. “strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.” A backbiting tongue overthrew the house of a great man, Onias, the real high priest.

precepts.text: A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many; strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men. Somebody that lies on you can do much destruction.
precepts.point: His master's wrath was kindled, and Joseph's master took him and put him into the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were bound. Remember how old Joseph is: 17.
precepts.why:
When Potiphar’s wife could not get her way, she lied. She called the men of her house and said, “See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us; he came in unto me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice.” Then “she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home”: she kept his clothes as false evidence, and told her husband the same lie.

Sirach shows what that kind of tongue does: “A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.” Somebody that lies on you can do much destruction. Joseph was the greatest man in Potiphar's house, trusted with everything, and a lying tongue brought him down to the king's prison.

It is the same today. Many brothers have been locked up because a woman lied on them: an ex-wife or ex-girlfriend who wants his life to go down the tubes, who calls him over, is refused, and then threatens to tell the police he hurt her. Others are in jail because a woman started a fight and expected him to defend her. Don't deal with a woman like that; that is the kind of woman Joseph had over him.

And this same spirit met our people in slavery. A lot of us were put to death because of it. Emmett Till was put to death for the lying woman, and there are a lot of cases like that. What Potiphar's wife did to Joseph, a backbiting tongue has done to Israel again and again.

precepts.text: Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue. The tongue does a lot of evil, and that's what Potiphar's wife did to Joseph.
precepts.point: His master's wrath was kindled, and Joseph's master took him and put him into the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were bound. Remember how old Joseph is: 17.
precepts.why:
Sirach goes on: “Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.” The tongue does a lot of evil, and that is exactly what Potiphar’s wife did to Joseph. She never lifted a sword against him; she only spoke, and her words did the work.

She told her husband, “The Hebrew servant, which thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me,” and “when his master heard the words of his wife,” “his wrath was kindled.” On nothing but her word, “Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound.” Remember how old Joseph is here: 17.

That is how our people have fallen too: brothers in prison on a lie, and in slavery times men like Emmett Till put to death because of a lying woman's words. More have fallen by the tongue than by the sword. Guard yourself from the kind of company that can destroy you with a word.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: One man beareth hatred against another, and doth he seek pardon from the Lord? You have hatred for your brother, for your wife, for the leadership, and you are asking the Lord for forgiveness? It is not going to work. He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself: who falls like you, who sins like you; and doth he ask forgiveness of his own sins?

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: If he that is but flesh nourish hatred, who will intreat for pardon of his sins? You cannot forgive your brother or your sister, Christ is not going to forgive you. Christ forgave us out of many idolatrous things and many sins, outside and inside this truth; we have to forgive our brothers the same way if we want that forgiveness.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: Remember thy end, and let enmity cease: at the end we are judged by what is in this Bible and what we did on this earth. Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to thy neighbour; remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance: if somebody offends you, brush it off your shoulders and let it go.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: Abstain from strife, and thou shalt diminish thy sins: for a furious man will kindle strife. A sinful man disquieteth friends, and maketh debate among them that be at peace: wherever the bitter brother goes he brings debate and chaos, vain arguments with no fruit. When it says disquiet, that is the feeling when the brother comes around and your defenses go up, because only bitter brothers come with strife; the brothers with peace come with the fruit of the spirit.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: He that revengeth shall find vengeance from the Lord, and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance. If you take vengeance, you will find vengeance from the Lord. If David had taken vengeance, he would have found vengeance from the Lord.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: Forgive thy neighbour the hurt that he hath done unto thee, so shall thy sins also be forgiven when thou prayest. We will do things that hurt each other from time to time; your spouse will do things that hurt you from time to time. Why does it say the hurt? Because it hurts, and you do not really want to forgive; it is hard. But you have to do what God says and get rid of that pride, because if you do not forgive them, it turns into bitterness. And it is not talking about forgiving only the small things you want to forgive; it is talking about the stuff that really hurt. King David forgave Saul for trying to kill him.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: One man beareth hatred against another, and doth he seek pardon from the Lord? You are bearing grudges and bitterness toward your spouse and talking about how you love God: you are phony and you are fake.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to thy neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at the ignorance. To wink at ignorance means sometimes people say dumb stuff out of immaturity; the person has not grown, and they probably did not even mean it a certain way. For the root of bitterness not to build up in you, sometimes you just wink at it: that person just does not know. Do not take it serious.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: Abstain from strife, and thou shalt diminish thy sins: for a furious man will kindle strife. Strife is the arguing. When you see brothers and sisters arguing and striving all the time, that is evil among them. Abstaining from strife is how you diminish your sins.
